query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A brief severe plastic deformation (cold rolling) followed by short-time annealing refines the lamellar colony architecture in eutectic high-entropy alloys, thus reducing microcrack susceptibility and simultaneously increasing tensile strength and room‐temperature ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high‐entropy alloy containing coarse, dual‐phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries where microcracking initiates under room-temperature tension.
generation.intervention: Apply a single processing step of severe plastic deformation (e.g. approximately 50% cold rolling reduction) immediately followed by a short-time annealing heat treatment designed to refine the lamellar spacing without triggering significant grain growth.
generation.conditions: Room-temperature tensile testing with processing parameters (cold rolling reduction and annealing time/temperature) tuned to avoid over-annealing or excessive deformation; the intervention is effective if applied within these controlled limits.
generation.structural_mediator: A refined microstructure characterized by a decreased lamellar colony size and narrower interlamellar spacing, along with improved interface coherence between phases.
generation.mechanism: The refined lamellar structure distributes stress more uniformly across both phases, mitigates stress concentrations at internal boundaries, and blunts crack initiation sites. This synergistic enhancement of interface bonding and disruption of critical microcrack pathways simultaneously elevates yield/ultimate strengths and delays crack propagation to improve ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, the treated alloy will exhibit higher yield and ultimate tensile strengths as well as improved elongation to failure (increased ductility) at room temperature.
generation.baseline: The conventional eutectic high-entropy alloy processed by standard methods, which shows brittleness and limited tensile deformation due to coarse lamellar colonies and numerous microcrack-prone boundaries.
generation.boundary: This intervention is effective only if the processing avoids excessive annealing (which could lead to grain coarsening) or over-deformation (which might induce damage); the improvements are expected within a narrow processing window where refinement is achieved without compromising phase integrity.
generation.uncertainty: While the mechanism suggests simultaneous improvement in strength and ductility, the exact processing parameters and the magnitude of the enhancement require precise tuning. Variations in alloy composition or unforeseen phase reactions during processing may also influence the results.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples from the same eutectic high-entropy alloy: one set using standard, conventional processing and the other set undergoing the proposed cold rolling (≈50% reduction) followed by short-time annealing. Characterize the microstructure (lamellar spacing, colony size, interface quality) by microscopy, then perform room-temperature tensile tests to measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation to failure.
measurements: Lamellar spacing and colony size via scanning/transmission electron microscopy
Yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation via standard tensile testing
Microcrack density and propagation behavior in fractured samples
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the processed samples do not show statistically significant improvements in both strength and ductility (i.e., yield/ultimate tensile strengths and elongation to failure) as compared to the conventionally processed baseline, or if microcrack analysis reveals no decrease in crack initiation and propagation, then the hypothesis is falsified.
